Definition: Sallu or Sallai, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Sallu is the name of two Israelites: Sallu the son of Meshullam, a Benjaminite who settled in Jerusalem after the return, and Sallu the priest, chief of the priests in the days of Jeshua. The same name serves a family returning home and a priesthood serving again.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God brings His people home to rebuild, and Sallu's two bearers — one a settler, one a priest — show both sides of that return.
RelatedPeople: Sallu, Son of Meshullam; Sallai the Priest
